verdict: Alnylam's drug sales jumped 52% as AMVUTTRA kept growing, but the headline $2.2B profit came almost entirely from a one-off $1.9B tax benefit — not from selling more medicine.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Inflated by the one-off tax benefit; non-GAAP EPS was $16.26

kpis.label: Cash & securities
kpis.note: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities at Sep 30, 2026

segments.name: AMVUTTRA
segments.note: Alnylam's biggest drug — a treatment for ATTR amyloidosis, a disease where a misfolded protein damages the heart and nerves. Growth is driven by patients with the heart form of the disease (ATTR-CM) in the US and new launches in Japan, Germany and Italy.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: Royalties Alnylam earns on other companies' sales — mainly Novartis's Leqvio, a cholesterol drug built on Alnylam's technology. It doubled as Leqvio sales grew.

segments.name: GIVLAARI
segments.note: A treatment for acute hepatic porphyria, a rare liver-related disorder. Sales rose as more patients started treatment.

segments.name: Collaboration revenue
segments.note: Payments from partners Roche and Regeneron for working together on new drugs. It fell sharply only because a year ago included a one-off $300M milestone payment from Roche.

segments.name: OXLUMO
segments.note: A treatment for primary hyperoxaluria, a rare kidney-stone disease. Sales were flat.

segments.name: ONPATTRO
segments.note: The older version of the ATTR treatment. Sales halved as patients switch to AMVUTTRA, its longer-lasting successor.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Running clinical trials — including the big TRITON studies of nucresiran — and developing new RNAi drugs (medicines that switch off disease-causing genes).

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the drugs worldwide, plus running the company — finance, legal and admin.

otherDetail: Other expense was $50.0M, net: $84.4M of interest expense (including $58M tied to the earlier sale of future Leqvio royalties and $23M for drug-development funding liabilities), partly offset by $30.9M of interest income and $3.4M of other income.
footerNote: Cost of revenue is cost of goods sold; the separate 'cost of collaborations and royalties' line was $0 in Q3 2026. Figures are as reported, in $M.
oneTimers: The $1,871.5M tax benefit — the reason net income hit $2,167.3M — came from releasing valuation allowances on US deferred tax assets: an accounting judgment that past tax losses and credits are now likely to be usable. It is non-cash and one-off; without it, net income would have been about $296M.
Collaboration revenue fell 80% only because Q3 2025 included a one-off $300M milestone payment from Roche when the first patient was dosed in the ZENITH trial of zilebesiran.

takeaways.title: A tax entry made the profit
takeaways.text: Net income was $2,167.3M, but $1,871.5M of it was a one-off tax benefit from releasing valuation allowances on deferred tax assets — paper profit, not cash from sales. Earnings per share of $15.72 carries the same boost.

takeaways.title: The drug business is booming
takeaways.text: Net product revenues rose 52% to $1,291.9M. AMVUTTRA alone brought in $1,130.4M, up 65%, as its use in the heart form of ATTR amyloidosis expanded; total TTR revenues were $1,150.0M, up 59%. Management kept its full-year 2026 guidance unchanged.

takeaways.title: Day-to-day profit actually fell
takeaways.text: Operating income slipped 6% to $345.8M despite higher sales. The cost of goods sold jumped 83% — AMVUTTRA carries a higher royalty rate on sales — and research spending rose 14% as big Phase 3 trials ramped up.
